name: desmatosuchus
_about: SCULPTED (2026-11-08, tools/creaturegen/prehistoric/desmatosuchus.py): DESMATOSUCHUS SPURENSIS, a late Triassic AETOSAUR (a pseudosuchian archosaur on the crocodiles' side, not a dinosaur), 4.5 m long and about a metre at the hips: a heavily armoured herbivore. The ARMOUR is rows of rectangular OSTEODERMS, each a `fin` plate laid on the probed skin -- rooted along its front edge just under it, its rim the exact rectangle, the rear edge standing proud so each row overlaps the next like tiles, a slab with a crisp edge and a dark rim band: one sheet a side a row, over the flat top of the back and down the flank's shoulder, from behind the skull down the neck, over the trunk and round the tail to near its tip, narrowing toward it. SPIKES (horns, faired, rising through their laterals): along the neck growing back to 20 cm, the great SHOULDER SPIKES (45 cm, broad and flattened at the root) out from the last cervical row rising out and up, then sweeping back (above the back in profile); short keels on every other lateral of the trunk and the tail's root. A small low head, the SHORT deep snout ending in a blunt UPTURNED spade (a pig's) with the nostrils on it, small leaf-shaped teeth (horns), a small eye; semi-erect legs (elbows and knees out, thick upper bones, short shins) on broad feet, five short clawed toes splayed forward; a long tapering tail held off the ground. Dull grey-brown, the plates paler with dark rims. Coats: grey-brown, ochre, slate; variant `juvenile` (.35).
